headline: No Kings rallies ask one thing: vote early.
summary: The No Kings network held hundreds of rallies across the US on Saturday, billed as nonpartisan and aimed at early voting in the November 3 midterms. At the Lincoln Memorial, a few hundred people in caps and coats danced to a band. Signs read "VOTE EARLY" and "HANDS OFF MY VOTE!" The network has marched against Trump for nearly two years.
cover_answer: Billed that way. Two years of marches against Trump.
table_question: A rally says it's for everyone but it's against one person. Is it?

5-7.script: Yesterday, in lots of cities, people stood together holding signs that said VOTE EARLY. Voting is how grown-ups pick who runs things, like when your class votes on a game. These people want everyone to vote soon instead of waiting. A band played, and people danced in the cold.
5-7.why: Signs, a band, dancing. Voting is the class picking a game. A six-year-old reasons from what they can see, so the signs come before the vote.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script hands them the signs, the band and the dancing before it says what a vote is, and the class picking a game is a vote they have already been in. The name of the group and who it opposes can wait. Expect "did you vote?" Tell them the truth, and when.

8-12.script: A group called No Kings held hundreds of rallies on Saturday. Their point: in America the president is not a king, and voting early proves it. The rallies were billed as nonpartisan, but the group has marched against Trump for two years. A club that says everyone is welcome, and has a side.
8-12.why: A name, a claim, a vote. Then the label beside the side.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out rules and whether people apply them to themselves, so the script gives them the chain, name to claim to vote, then the label the rallies chose, nonpartisan, beside two years spent against one president. The club that says everyone is welcome is one they know. Expect "is it fair to call it that?" Let them decide.

13-17.script: Can a rally be nonpartisan when its network has marched against one president for two years? Saturday's rallies said vote early. Second: the Justice Department warned officials who count ballots from suspected noncitizens of prosecution. Who is told to use their power, and who to fear it?
13-17.why: Nonpartisan and against Trump, both on the record. Then the warning.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: the rallies were billed as nonpartisan, and the network has opposed Trump for two years. The script sets that beside the Justice Department's warning to ballot counters and asks who is encouraged and who is warned. Expect "will they take ballots?" Three senators asked for a promise. No answer yet.

5-7.a: Not until you are 18. You can come with me when I do, and see how it works.

8-12.a: That a president is not a king. The group has opposed Trump for two years.

8-12.q: Why vote early instead of on the day?
8-12.a: The story doesn't say. The signs read VOTE EARLY.

13-17.a: Organizers billed it that way. AP counts nearly two years of marches.
Three senators asked for a promise it won't. No answer in the story.
